setting: The colony world is not wild — it is being deliberately cultivated. Life here is too convenient, too AIMED: rivers run to the right places, soils self-enrich, blights arrive only to be answered. The gardeners are present and acting NOW but never seen — only sensed, as a faint aimed-ness in things and a pressure of attention when a tool is used. The artifacts are their shaping-tools, seeded into the soil to steer evolution; the resource is the engineered biosphere itself. The ordered chain is PROSPECTIVE and INWARD: each tool used, each lineage cultivated, reveals one more step of the gardeners' METHOD and what we are being grown INTO. The climax is not a fall — it is the harvest the gardeners have been patiently waiting for, still unfolding. The open question per world: are the colonists a welcome guest, a pest to be culled, or the next thing being grown?

civs.name: the-gardeners
civs.trait: present and acting, never seen — they shape the world by hand and watch; you feel their attention, never their bodies

civs.name: the-loam-tenders
civs.trait: a lesser hidden caste that maintains the soil-shrines and gene-looms between the gardeners' great workings

civs.name: the-first-cultivars
civs.trait: an earlier lineage the gardeners grew to sapience here, then either harvested or moved on — the precedent the colony is unknowingly repeating

climax_label: the harvest the gardeners are waiting for
